title: Atlas of Care (formerly Atlas of Caregiving) and its Atlas CareMap
what: An organisation that designed tools and educational programmes to help people see and talk about how they care for themselves and those around them. Its Atlas CareMap is a hand-drawn diagram of one person's care relationships, showing who cares for whom and how.
quote: The Atlas CareMap is a diagram of a person’s care ecosystem, drawn by hand, showing who cares for whom, and how.
status: Shut down at the end of 2025; the About page says the website is still maintained by Rajiv Mehta to keep its tools and research available.
notes: NAME COLLISION: this organisation calls itself 'Atlas of Care' on its own site (footer '© 2020 Atlas of Care'). About page wording is 'Atlas of Care (formally “Atlas of Caregiving”) shutdown at the end of 2025, a decade after its founding' [sic]. Rajiv Mehta is listed as Founder & CEO. Founding year is not stated as a number. The CareMap page says its two booklets were 'Published in 2019'. Saved: atlasofcaregiving_about.txt, atlasofcaregiving_home.txt, atlasofcaregiving_caremap.txt.

title: EU Care Atlas
publisher: Foundation for European Progressive Studies (FEPS) and Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung (FES)
what: An online data tool launched by FEPS and FES ahead of International Women's Day 2022. It presents the gender overall earnings gap and gender gaps in time spent on paid and unpaid work, as an EU average and for EU member states; FES reports a 2024 update adding data on early childhood education and care and on long-term care.
quote: maps how care deficits directly relate to inequality
status: Updated in March 2024 according to the FES page.
notes: The atlas tool itself was not opened in this run; the description rests on the FEPS launch notice (dated 03/03/2022) and the FES update notice (dated 05.03.2024). Whether the data is shown on a geographic map is not confirmed from the fetched pages. Saved: eucareatlas_feps.txt, eucareatlas_fes.txt, eucareatlas_page.txt.

title: Mapa de Cuidados de México (MACU)
publisher: Instituto Nacional de las Mujeres, ONU Mujeres, Centro Global de Excelencia en Estadísticas de Género, and a research team at El Colegio de México
what: An interactive map of care services in Mexico. It lets people find care centres for children, older people and people with disabilities, and gives indicators of care supply, potential demand and accessibility at national, state and municipal level, built from georeferenced INEGI data (the DENUE directory of establishments, the 2020 census and 2020 urban-environment data).
quote: Es una plataforma digital interactiva que ofrece información infográfica sobre la oferta, demanda e infraestructura de cuidados a nivel nacional, estatal y municipal
notes: Year is the footer date ('©MACU - Mapa de Cuidados para México | 2023'); the page also says DENUE data are updated to March 2024 and that an observatory was added to the platform in 2024. The page cites 'Sánchez, Aparicio y Herrera (2024)' for the study, which was not fetched. Saved: mx_mapacuidados.txt.

title: Care Georeferencing Tool (Mapping Care: Innovative tools for georeferencing care supply and demand)
what: A tool developed by the Gender Team of UNDP-LAC for building care maps: it records the care services available in a city or area, maps where people who need or may need care live, and compares the two. The page names Colombia, Uruguay and the Dominican Republic, and lists the District Government of Bogota as a past partner.
quote: aims to facilitate the construction of care maps
notes: No year on the page. The tool's pages on undp.org returned 403 in this run, so the description rests on UNDP's Digital X catalogue page only. Saved: undp_digitalx_care.txt.

title: Mutual Aid Wiki
publisher: Mutual Aid Wiki (open-source project; repository Covid-Mutual-Aid/mutual-aid-wiki)
what: A map and dataset of mutual aid groups around the world that combines community-maintained lists with individual submissions; groups can add and edit their own information and draw the area they cover. Its README says it began as a map synced with a spreadsheet of UK mutual aid groups and started with covidmutualaid.org.
quote: This resource combines community maintained sources with individual submissions to provide a unified source of information on mutual aid groups.
status: Site returned its app page (title 'Mutual Aid Wiki', description 'Community created map of Mutual Aid groups throughout the world') at fetch; whether the data is still maintained is not stated.
notes: The site is a script-loaded app, so the description comes from the project's README (fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com; the github.com repository page itself was not reachable from this session). No dates in the README. WARNING: covidmutualaid.org, named in the README, served an unrelated gambling page at fetch; do not link it. Saved: mutualaidwiki_readme.txt, mutualaidwiki_home.txt.

title: Reach4Help: Global Map of Aid
what: A volunteer-run initiative that maps organisations and groups around the world offering aid. Its home page describes a 'Global Map of 10K+ Aid Organizations' and says it connects mutual aid movements to people in need 'through the COVID-19 pandemic and beyond'.
quote: Map of organizations and groups around the world offering aid and assistance to those in need throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, Ukranian refugee crises and other disasters
status: Site online at fetch; home page footer is dated 2022.
notes: The quote is the map page's own meta description, spelling as on the page ('Ukranian'). The map page's social title is 'COVID-19 Mutual Aid Map - Reach4Help'. The map data loads by script and was not read. No founding year on the fetched pages. Saved: reach4help_map.txt, reach4help_home.txt.

title: Open Referral: Human Services Data Specification (HSDS)
what: An initiative that develops data standards and open-source tools for sharing information about health, human and social services. Its Human Services Data Specification (HSDS) sets out a data model and API for publishing such service directories; the documentation fetched is for version 3.0.1.
quote: Open Referral develops data standards and open source tools that make it easier to share, find and use information about health, human, and social services.
status: Website and documentation online at fetch (documentation version 3.0.1).
notes: No founding year on the fetched pages. Saved: openreferral_docs.txt, openreferral_home.txt.

title: Atlas of Utopias
what: A collection of case stories of community-led changes to water, energy, housing and food systems, made up of the finalists of the Transformative Cities People's Choice Award. The page says it is a sample chosen by peer review, not a comprehensive mapping of such practices.
quote: The Atlas of Utopias showcases collective transformations that ensure access to basic rights: water, energy, housing and food.
status: Online at fetch; the site menu lists award editions 2018, 2019, 2020 and ’21–’22.
notes: No single publication year. The About page describes Transformative Cities as 'a platform facilitated by several international partners' without naming them in the text read; a contact address at tni.org appears there. Saved: atlasofutopias.txt, transformativecities_about.txt.

title: Sistema Distrital de Cuidado (Manzanas del Cuidado), Bogotá
what: The website of Bogotá's district care system, which it describes as spaces to recognise, redistribute and reduce the load of care work on women. It offers a directory and a map of the active Manzanas del Cuidado.
quote: Encuentra en este mapa las Manzanas del Cuidado activas en Bogotá.
notes: https://manzanasdelcuidado.gov.co/ redirects to this address. No start year on the page read. Saved: bogota_sidicu.txt.

title: Mutual Aid Hub
what: A website for finding mutual aid networks and other community self-support projects near the user, and for joining them, offering resources or submitting requests.
quote: Find Mutual Aid Networks and other community self-support projects near you.
status: Site returned its app page at fetch; whether the listings are maintained is not stated.
notes: Only the page's meta description could be read (script-loaded app). The page source contains the string 'townhallproject', but who runs the site was not confirmed in readable text. No dates. Saved: mutualaidhub_home.txt.

title: Vikalp Sangam
what: A website documenting grassroots and policy alternatives in India across many fields; the name is Hindi for 'Alternatives Confluence'. The site offers its stories by map and by location.
quote: The name ‘Vikalp Sangam’ is Hindi for ‘Alternatives Confluence’.
notes: No start year confirmed from the page text read. Saved: vikalpsangam_about.txt.

title: If Women Counted: A New Feminist Economics
what: A book on sex discrimination in national income accounting, as its library record classes it. The first edition has an introduction by Gloria Steinem. Only the catalogue record was read.
notes: Catalogue records only: the Internet Archive item record (creator 'Waring, Marilyn, 1952-', title 'If women counted : a new feminist economics', publisher 'San Francisco : Harper & Row', date 1988, LCCN 88045160) and the Open Library editions list. The book's text was not read, so its argument is not summarised here. The record was fetched through https://archive.org/metadata/ifwomencountedne00wari, which is the data behind the public page given as url. Saved: ia_record_ifwomencountedne00wari.txt, waring_ol_editions.txt, waring_openlibrary.txt.

authors: Laura Addati, Umberto Cattaneo, Valeria Esquivel and Isabel Valarino
title: Care work and care jobs for the future of decent work
what: An ILO report on unpaid and paid care work and its relationship with the world of work, with a focus on gender inequalities in households and the labour market. The ILO page says it draws on data from over 90 countries and covers policy in five areas: care, macroeconomics, labour, social protection and migration.
quote: This report takes a comprehensive look at unpaid and paid care work and its relationship with the changing world of work.
notes: Publication date on the page: 28 June 2018. ISBN print 9789221316428. The report PDF itself was not opened. Saved: ilo_carework_2018.txt.

title: SDG indicator metadata: Indicator 5.4.1: Proportion of time spent on unpaid domestic and care work, by sex, age and location
publisher: United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD) and UN Women (custodian agencies)
what: The official metadata sheet for Sustainable Development Goal indicator 5.4.1. It defines the indicator as the proportion of time in a day that men and women spend on unpaid domestic and care work, using the activity divisions of the International Classification of Activities for Time-Use Statistics 2016 (ICATUS 2016).
quote: Proportion of time spent on unpaid domestic and care work, by sex, age and location
notes: Year left blank because the document is a living metadata sheet; the only date on it is the last-updated date. Saved: sdg541_meta.txt.

authors: Coffey, Clare; Espinoza Revollo, Patricia; Harvey, Rowan; Lawson, Max; Parvez Butt, Anam; Piaget, Kim; Sarosi, Diana; Thekkudan, Julie
title: Time to Care: Unpaid and underpaid care work and the global inequality crisis
what: An Oxfam report that sets extreme wealth against the unpaid and underpaid care work done mainly by women and girls, and calls on governments to invest in national care systems and introduce progressive taxation.
quote: the unpaid and underpaid care work done primarily by women and girls around the world
notes: Author names are in the order and form the Oxfam page lists them; the page also lists Editor: Seery, Emma. Page date 20/01/2020; DOI 10.21201/2020.5419; ISBN 978-1-78748-541-9. The report PDF itself was not opened. Saved: oxfam_timetocare_pp.txt, oxfam_timetocare.txt.

title: Counting Women's Work
publisher: Counting Women's Work, a project within the National Transfer Accounts research project (site copyright 2017 University of Cape Town)
what: An international research project that measures the gendered economy, including unpaid care work. It uses time-use data to build National Time Transfer Accounts, which estimate production, consumption and transfers of unpaid care and household work by age and sex, alongside the market economy.
quote: It is through measurement that we begin to value the role of care in society
status: Website online at fetch; whether the project is still producing estimates is not stated on the pages read.
notes: No start year on the fetched pages; the footer reads 'Copyright © 2017 University of Cape Town'. Saved: countingwomenswork.txt, countingwomenswork_about.txt.

title: Progress of the world’s women 2019–2020: Families in a changing world
what: An edition of UN Women's periodic flagship report. It assesses families in the context of economic, demographic, political and social change, with global, regional and national data, and covers family laws, employment, unpaid care work, violence against women, and migration.
notes: Publication year on the page: 2019. The series page also lists the 2015–2016 edition, 'Transforming economies, realizing rights'. Saved: unwomen_progress_2019_2020.txt, unwomen_progress_2019.txt, unwomen_progress_2015.txt.

title: For Love and Money: Care Provision in the United States
what: An edited volume on paid and unpaid care work in the United States, including a chapter estimating how much unpaid care is provided.
notes: Publication date on the publisher page: August 2012; ISBN 978-0-87154-353-0. Saved: folbre_rsf.txt.

title: Human Development Report 1995: Gender and Human Development
what: The 1995 edition of UNDP's annual report. Its page says it analyses progress in reducing gender disparities, introduces two measures for ranking countries on gender equality (GEM and GDI), and analyses the under-valuation and non-recognition of women's work.
quote: Human Development, if not engendered, is endangered.
notes: The report PDF was not opened, so no figure for the value of unpaid work is given. Saved: hdr1995.txt.

title: Toward a Feminist Theory of Caring
publisher: State University of New York Press
what: A chapter in Circles of Care: Work and Identity in Women's Lives, edited by Emily K. Abel and Margaret K. Nelson. The sentence quoted here is in the 1990 book; the chapter itself could not be opened to confirm its page.
quote: includes everything that we do to maintain, continue, and repair our “world” so that we can live in it
notes: The quote was string-matched in the snippet returned by the Internet Archive full-text search restricted to the scanned book (item circlesofcarewor0000unse, State University of New York Press, 1990). The snippet does not give a page number, the scan is OCR text, and the chapter itself could not be opened (lending-restricted), so the attribution of the sentence to this chapter rests on the book match plus the lead; the sentence before and after the snippet was not seen. SUNY's page dates the paperback July 1990. Saved: circlesofcare_suny.txt, ia_fulltext_search_circlesofcare_quote.txt, ia_record_circlesofcarewor0000unse.txt.

title: Matters of Care: Speculative Ethics in More than Human Worlds
what: A book that treats care as an ethical and political obligation in the worlds of technoscience and naturecultures, and argues that care is not something only humans do.
quote: Matters of Care contests the view that care is something only humans do
notes: Publication date on the publisher page: March 21st, 2017; ISBN 9781517900656. Saved: puig_umn.txt.

title: Hail the maintainers
what: An essay arguing that maintenance matters more to most lives than innovation does. The page's browser title is 'Innovation is overvalued. Maintenance often matters more'.
quote: Capitalism excels at innovation but is failing at maintenance, and for most lives it is maintenance that matters more
notes: Date on the page: 7 April 2016. The quote is the essay's standfirst. Saved: russell_vinsel_aeon.txt.

title: MANIFESTO FOR MAINTENANCE ART 1969!
publisher: Queens Museum (exhibition page for 'Mierle Laderman Ukeles: Maintenance Art', which links a scan of the manifesto)
what: A manifesto by the artist Mierle Laderman Ukeles. The Queens Museum, which showed a survey of her work from 09.18.16 to 02.19.17, describes it as setting out the hidden but essential role of maintenance in Western society.
quote: laid out the hidden, yet essential role of maintenance in Western society
notes: The quote is the museum's description, not the manifesto's own words. The year is taken from the title as the museum gives it. The museum's PDF of the manifesto (https://queensmuseum.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/04/Ukeles-Manifesto-for-Maintenance-Art-1969_5-pages.pdf) downloaded but is a page scan with no readable text, so nothing is quoted from it. Saved: ukeles_queens.txt.

title: Leverage Points: Places to Intervene in a System
what: A paper on leverage points, which it describes as places in a complex system where a small shift in one thing can produce big changes in everything. It sets out a numbered list of twelve places to intervene in a system, 'in increasing order of effectiveness'.
quote: a small shift in one thing can produce big changes in everything
notes: Year and publisher come from the PDF edition on the same site (https://donellameadows.org/wp-content/userfiles/Leverage_Points.pdf): '© The Sustainability Institute, 1999. A shorter version of this paper appeared in Whole Earth, winter 1997.' The PDF byline reads 'by Donella H. Meadows'. Saved: meadows_leverage.txt, meadows_pdf.txt.

title: Revolution at Point Zero: Housework, Reproduction, and Feminist Struggle, Second Edition
what: A collection of essays written between 1974 and 2016 on housework, social reproduction and women's struggles over them. The publisher says it begins with Federici's organising work in the Wages for Housework movement and goes on to the globalisation of care work, the crisis of elder care and the politics of the commons.
quote: collects four decades of research and theorizing on the nature of housework, social reproduction, and women’s struggles on this terrain
notes: Year is that of the second edition ('Published: 7/2020' on the publisher page); the first edition's date is not on the page. Saved: federici_pmpress3.txt.

title: Moral Boundaries: A Political Argument for an Ethic of Care
what: A book of political theory on care. The publisher says it contests the association of care with women and argues that care cannot be a useful moral and political concept until its association with a 'women's morality' is challenged.
quote: Moral Boundaries contests the association of care with women as empirically and historically inaccurate, as well as politically unwise.
notes: Publisher page: 'Copyright 1993', 1st Edition. The quote is publisher's description. The Internet Archive record also gives New York : Routledge, 1993. Saved: tronto_routledge.txt, ia_record_moralboundariesp0000tron.txt.

title: The Care Manifesto: The Politics of Interdependence
what: A book arguing that care should be placed at the centre of politics, the state and the economy.
quote: Our lives are always interdependent.
notes: The Verso page lists a paperback of September 2020 (128 pages, ISBN 9781839760969) and a further paperback edition dated September 2026; the description shown is for the 2026 edition. Individual members of the collective are not named in the text read. Saved: caremanifesto_verso.txt.

title: The Maintainers
what: A research and practice network concerned with maintenance, infrastructure, repair and the labour that sustains the human-built world. Its page says it started in 2015 and held in-person conferences until 2019.
quote: a global research and practice network interested in the concepts of maintenance, infrastructure, repair, and the myriad forms of labor and expertise that sustain our human-built world
status: The page says it continues as a network-led model, stewarded by a steering committee and fiscally hosted by the Raft Foundation.
notes: Year is the start year given on the page. Founders are not named in the passage read. Saved: maintainers_about.txt.

title: Maintenance and Care
what: An article in Places Journal, published on 20 November 2018. Only its bibliographic record was read.
notes: METADATA ONLY. placesjournal.org returned 403 to every fetch in this run, so the article was not read and its content is not described; details are from the Crossref record for DOI 10.22269/181120 (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.22269/181120). Check the article by hand before citing more than the bibliographic line. Saved: mattern_crossref.txt.

title: Governing the Commons: The Evolution of Institutions for Collective Action
what: A study of how natural resources used by many people in common are governed. It describes three models often used to justify state or market solutions, sets out alternatives, and examines successful and unsuccessful cases, among them communal tenure in meadows and forests, irrigation communities and fisheries.
quote: common pool problems sometimes are solved by voluntary organisations rather than by a coercive state
notes: Publication date on the page: 30 November 1990. The quote is from the publisher's abstract, not the book's text. The publisher page names 'irrigation communities' but not the zanjeras or huertas, so those are not asserted here. Saved: ostrom_cup.txt.

title: Diverse Economies Iceberg
what: An image, licensed CC BY-SA 4.0, that pictures economic practices as an iceberg: what is usually called 'the economy' is the tip, and a wider range of practices lies below. The Community Economies site says its approach builds on J.K. Gibson-Graham's feminist critique of political economy.
quote: What is usually referred to as “the economy” is just the tip of this diverse economy iceberg.
status: Online at fetch; the page calls it 'the most up-to-date version'.
notes: The page asks to be cited as 'Diverse Economies Iceberg by Community Economies Collective'; it does not credit J.K. Gibson-Graham by name for the image and gives no date of first publication. Related books confirmed on the University of Minnesota Press site: J. K. Gibson-Graham, A Postcapitalist Politics (published March 17th, 2006), and Take Back the Economy with Jenny Cameron and Stephen Healy (2013). Saved: gibsongraham_iceberg.txt, cec_about.txt, gg_postcapitalist_umn.txt, gg_takeback_umn.txt.

title: Whose Woods Are These? Counter-Mapping Forest Territories in Kalimantan, Indonesia
what: A journal article on counter-mapping forest territories, in Antipode volume 27, issue 4, pages 383 to 406. Only its bibliographic record was read.
notes: Metadata only: the Wiley article page returned 403, so details come from the Crossref record for the DOI (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1111/j.1467-8330.1995.tb00286.x), where the title is in capitals. The article was not read, so its content is not described. The DOI link in url was not itself opened. Saved: peluso_crossref.txt.

title: Anti-Eviction Mapping Project
what: A volunteer collective that makes digital maps, software, oral-history and video work, murals and reports about dispossession and resistance in gentrifying places, working mainly in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles and New York City.
quote: a data-visualization, critical cartography, and multimedia storytelling collective documenting dispossession and resistance upon gentrifying landscapes
status: Described in the present tense on its own page at fetch.
notes: No founding year on the fetched pages. Saved: aemp_about.txt, aemp_home.txt.

title: Native Land Digital (Native-Land.ca)
what: An Indigenous-led not-for-profit organisation based in Canada that runs Native-Land.ca, a resource for learning about Indigenous territories, languages, lands and ways of life. It says it uses oral histories, maps and written records and does not claim to define territories.
quote: Native Land Digital does not claim to define territories—it provides a starting point for deeper conversations and engagement with Indigenous communities.
notes: The address https://native-land.ca/about/ redirects to the url given. No founding year on the fetched pages. Saved: nativeland_about.txt, nativeland_home.txt.

title: Seeing Like a State: How Certain Schemes to Improve the Human Condition Have Failed
what: A book analysing failed large-scale state plans. The publisher says Scott argues that centrally managed plans misfire when they impose schematic visions on complex interdependencies, and that local, practical knowledge matters as much as formal knowledge.
quote: local, practical knowledge is as important as formal, epistemic knowledge
notes: The year is the paperback date on the publisher page ('Published: Monday, 8 Feb 1999'); the lead's earlier hardcover date could not be confirmed (the hardcover page had no details). A review quoted on the page uses the phrase 'simplify and make legible'. Saved: scott_yale.txt.

title: Commonwealth
what: The book that concludes the trilogy begun with Empire and continued in Multitude. The publisher says it argues for the idea of the 'common' in place of the opposition of private and public.
quote: They argue for the idea of the “common” to replace the opposition of private and public and the politics predicated on that opposition.
notes: The year is the paperback date on the publisher page ('Publication date: 04/15/2011'); the lead's 2009 first-edition date is not on the page and the hardcover page returned 404, so 2009 is unverified. Saved: hardtnegri_hup.txt.

title: This Is Not an Atlas
what: A book and website gathering more than 40 counter-cartographies from around the world, showing maps made as part of political struggle, critical research, art and education. Its contents include a piece on mapping the anti-eviction struggle in the San Francisco Bay Area.
quote: This Is Not an Atlas gathers more than 40 counter-cartographies from all over the world.
status: Online at fetch, with an open-access e-book offered.
notes: Editors, publisher and year are not in the page text read (the editorial is credited to Severin Halder and Boris Michel), so they are left out. Saved: notanatlas.txt.

title: An Atlas of Commoning
what: A touring exhibition, described as an ifa exhibition in collaboration with ARCH+, whose German premiere ran at Kunstraum Kreuzberg/Bethanien in Berlin from June 23 to August 26, 2018.
quote: An ifa exhibition in collaboration with ARCH+
notes: ifa's own page returned a bot check, so the description rests on the ARCH+ page. What 'ifa' stands for and the exhibition's subtitle are not asserted. Saved: atlasofcommoning_archplus.txt.
